outline:
本課程旨在進一步提升學生於學術會議與研討場合中以英語進行口頭報告、簡報發表及互動應對之能力。課程聚焦學術會議常見之發表形式，包括論文口頭發表、海報發表、研究摘要說明、短講及問答交流，並著重學術口語論述之組織、研究重點之清楚傳達、論點整合、聽眾互動與現場應答技巧。透過會議情境模擬、口頭報告、海報發表演練與回應活動，學生將強化其學術英語口語表達、簡報呈現與會議溝通能力，並建立參與國際學術交流之實務基礎。
This course aims to further develop students’ ability to deliver oral reports, conference presentations, and academic briefings in English in conference and seminar settings. It focuses on common forms of academic conference communication, including paper presentations, poster sessions, research summaries, short talks, and question-and-answer exchanges. Special emphasis is placed on organizing academic oral discourse, presenting research clearly, integrating key arguments, engaging with audiences, and responding effectively in live academic settings. Through conference simulations, oral presentation practice, poster presentation tasks, and response activities, students will strengthen their spoken academic English, presentation delivery, and conference communication skills, building a practical foundation for participation in international academic events.
schedule:
First half: selected Professional English in Use: Management readings and BESTEP practice. Second half: BESTEP academic presentation skills, especially Unit 6 summarising/paraphrasing and Unit 7 integrating text and visuals, applied to the course projects.

Week 1 (07 Sep–13 Sep 2026): Orientation, diagnostic work and research introduction.

Week 2 (14 Sep–20 Sep 2026): Management vocabulary and presentation foundations; research activities.

Week 3 (21 Sep–27 Sep 2026): Screening ideas and communicating proposals; research activities.

Week 4 (28 Sep–04 Oct 2026): Chart explanation and speaking practice; research activities.

Week 5 (05 Oct–11 Oct 2026): Innovation and collaborative language work; research activities.

Week 6 (12 Oct–18 Oct 2026): Management Units 6–7 review; BESTEP summarising and paraphrasing; handwritten eight-line group script without AI.

Week 7 (19 Oct–25 Oct 2026): 21 October: independent impromptu creative writing and research activity.

Week 8 (26 Oct–01 Nov 2026): 28 October: thesis-statement practice and essay writing, following the existing Classroom assignments.

Week 9 (2–8 November 2026): Midterm examination week; university common English examination on 3 November. No separate course midterm grade.

Week 10 (11 November 2026): BESTEP Unit 6: summarising and paraphrasing for an audience.
Activity: review the existing script and essay after feedback; identify the main point and supporting evidence for a presentation.

Week 11 (18 November 2026): BESTEP Unit 7: integrating text and visuals.
Activity: adapt a paragraph from the existing essay into an academic presentation introduction; explain its claim and supporting visual.

Week 12 (25 November 2026): BESTEP visual-information skills: explain a chart or diagram and connect it to a claim.
Activity: short team briefing with a visual and audience Q&A; feedback on the introduction.

Week 13 (2 December 2026): Academic presentation structure: opening, main points, signposting and conclusion.
Activity: revise the script and data commentary after feedback; practise explaining a slide without reading it aloud.

Week 14 (9 December 2026): BESTEP text/visual integration in the final presentation.
Activity: rehearsal, source attribution, transitions and audience questions.

Week 15 (16 December 2026): Final group academic presentations (8–10 minutes). Every member speaks; clear visual explanation and two audience questions; recorded presentation.

Week 16 (23 December 2026): Final submission of slides, script or speaking notes, and annotated outline; file-access checks. Submission period only.
scorePolicy:
Percentages of the final semester grade:
Coursework: 36%
speaking tasks: 12%
writing tasks: 12%
Attendance: 12%
Final presentation: 24%
Cool English independent learning, Weeks 17–18: 20%
University common English examination: 20%
Total: 100%.

Speaking (12%): assessed post-midterm briefings, Q&A and speaking practice. Writing (12%): post-midterm revisions and adaptations of the existing script and essay, including presentation notes/data commentary. Before-midterm coursework uses the announced attendance arrangement. Earlier research and practice tasks remain learning records.

Group assignments use the announced scale: 80 for submission, 90–95 for more complete work and 100 for the most complete work; members receive the same group score. The final presentation retains its combined 24% rubric and this group scale. Research extra credit follows the separate course announcement.

Skill evidence: at least three assessed speaking outputs and two writing outputs, including revision after feedback, drawn from the scheduled course tasks.
Speaking criteria: Content and Task Fulfillment; Organization and Coherence; Language Use; Delivery and Fluency; Interaction and Response.
Writing criteria: Content and Task Fulfillment; Organization and Coherence; Language Use; Genre and Professional Appropriacy; Revision and Development.
Assessments use the official four-level descriptors. At least one speaking assessment covers all five dimensions; interaction is marked N/A when inapplicable to another task.

Graded tasks within each coursework skill component are averaged equally. A draft and its revision count as one writing task. Midterm and final components are counted separately. Attendance begins at 100: the first three absences have no deduction, then five attendance points are deducted per additional absence. Approved leave follows university rules.

【BESTEP與英語能力認列】

BESTEP Speaking and Writing: 17 October 2026.
BESTEP Listening and Reading: 21 November 2026.
University common English examination: 3 November 2026, 10:10–11:25; separate 20% semester component.

Actual BESTEP participation earns 10 bonus points; an eligible other English proficiency test earns 5. Submit the required evidence by the end of the semester. Each score report is counted once, and the semester grade is capped at 100.

A verified B2 speaking or writing result may satisfy the designated 10 percentage points for that skill. The remaining 2 points in a 12-point allocation, or 6 in a 16-point allocation, are assessed through course work. Students continue to participate in the learning activities and complete the other requirements.
materials:
First-half textbook: Arthur McKeown and Ros Wright, Professional English in Use: Management, Cambridge University Press, 2011; selected readings, including Units 6–7, for vocabulary, discussion and project preparation.
Second-half teaching materials: EAP Power Up: Synthesizing Textual and Visual Information for Academic Success, Language Training & Testing Center (LTTC), 2024 (BESTEP); selected visual-information activities, Unit 6 summarising/paraphrasing and Unit 7 integrating text and visuals, adapted to academic presentations.
Writing reference: Joseph M. Williams and Joseph Bizup, Style: Lessons in Clarity and Grace, 11th edition, selected Lessons 1–3 and accompanying exercises.
Additional materials: instructor-prepared slides, task sheets and assessment rubrics; cited news/data sources; Cool English online exercises.
remarks: 本課程為專業英文（ESP/EAP）課程，教材、講義及簡報均採全英文；課堂授課及師生互動之英語使用比例90% (含)以上。
resources:
● 混成學習 (Blended Learning)
課程結合實體授課與線上學習（同步視訊／非同步活動）。
Combines face-to-face instruction with online learning (including synchronous video sessions or asynchronous activities).
● 參與式創新教學 (Participatory & Innovative Teaching)
強調學生參與與產出，導入翻轉、PBL/專題、設計思考或遊戲化等策略。
Emphasizes student engagement and outcomes by adopting strategies such as Flipped Classroom, PBL (Problem/Project- Based Learning), Design Thinking, or Gamification.
● 數位教材資源應用 (Application of Digital Resources)
採用影音多媒體或具開放授權之資源（如OCW、開放教科書）作為主要或輔助教材。
Adopts multimedia or open-licensed resources (e.g., OCW, Open Textbooks) as primary or supplementary teaching materials.
● 數位科技融入 (Digital Technology Integration)
運用生成式AI、VR/AR、IoT、IRS等新興科技輔助教學與評量。
Utilizes emerging technologies such as Generative AI, VR/AR, IoT, and IRS (Interactive Response Systems) to facilitate teaching and assessment.
